findings.issue_text: [BUG] The five new test methods reference an undeclared `realm` variable (e.g. `realm.admin().clients().findByClientId("myclient")`, `createUserPolicy(realm, client, ...)`, `realmAdminClient.realm(realm.getName())`), but the added field block declares only realmAdminClient/realmClient/clientsType, no `@InjectRealm ManagedRealm realm` field is added here or to the superclass AbstractPermissionTest (whose only injected field is `client`), and no InjectRealm/ManagedRealm import is added to PermissionClientTest — the symbol cannot resolve. tests/base fails to compile with 'cannot find symbol: variable realm' in every new test method (testManageOnlyOneClient, testConfigureOnlyOneClient, testManageAllClients, testViewAllClients, testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient), blocking the module build and CI until a `@InjectRealm ManagedRealm realm;` field plus the InjectRealm and ManagedRealm imports are added.

[ADVISORY] The javadoc added in this diff documents the void enforcing methods requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() as "Returns {@code true} if ..." instead of "Throws ForbiddenException if ... returns {@code false}", contradicting the contract written for the sibling require* methods in the same hunk (requireList, requireManage, requireListClientScopes, requireManageClientScopes). Implementers of the interface and callers reading the published contract misread requireView()/requireViewClientScopes() as boolean queries rather than enforcers that throw ForbiddenException, and the same method family now carries two conflicting specification styles that will drift further with each added method.

[ADVISORY] ClientPermissionsV2 ships dead code copied from the V1 implementation: the private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) method has no caller anywhere in the class (its only prospective caller, canExchangeTo, throws UnsupportedOperationException on entry), the `logger` field is never used, and the static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE is unused. Maintainers are misled into believing V2 wires up a token-exchange evaluation context (the kc.client.id attribute plumbing) and that token-exchange scopes are part of the V2 client schema, when canExchangeTo explicitly rejects them; the dead members must be carried through every future refactor of this class.

[ADVISORY] The evaluate-and-match-scope block is triplicated within this new class: hasPermission(ClientModel,String), hasPermission(String) and hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String) each re-implement root.evaluatePermission(...) followed by an iterate-permissions/iterate-scopes match against a single expected scope (the latter two sites sit at ~lines 240-251 and ~265-277 of the same new file). A future change to how granted scopes are matched (e.g. deny handling or multi-scope checks) has to be replicated in three places in this file; missing one makes list filtering via getClientsWithPermission disagree with the direct can* checks for the same caller and scope.

[BUG] The removal-event cleanup is now gated solely on the V1 flag (Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so deleting a client in a realm running the V2 feature (which this PR's ClientPermissionsV2 serves) performs no authorization cleanup at all, because the only handler would call ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (ClientPermissionsV2.java:193-195), which throws UnsupportedOperationException. The Resource and permission policies created for a client via getOrCreateResource/resolveClient (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:175-184, exercised by PermissionClientTest's createPermission calls) are orphaned forever in the realm's admin-permissions resource server when the client is deleted: getClientsWithPermission keeps iterating dead resources on every filtered client listing, the store accumulates stale entries with no V2 API to purge them (getPermissions/setPermissionsEnabled throw), and the same skip applies to realms that enabled V1 FGAP earlier and later turned the flag off. The diff ships the write path for client authorization resources without any delete path.

[ADVISORY] The private method getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) has zero call sites in the class (canExchangeTo at line 148 throws instead of using it), making it dead code together with the ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext/EvaluationContext imports and the unused logger field at line 51. Future maintainers reading the class can assume a token-exchange evaluation context exists and is wired up, when it is not; deleting the method removes 11 lines and three imports with no behavior change.

[ADVISORY] The CLIENTS resource type silently drops the token-exchange capability that V1 client permissions support: AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:70) omits the token-exchange scope, canExchangeTo/exchangeToPermission and the whole V1 per-client permission-management surface (isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) throw UnsupportedOperationException, and the static import of TOKEN_EXCHANGE at line 46 is unused — corroborating that the scope was considered and dropped without a replacement. Realms migrating from V1 fine-grained authz to V2 silently lose token-exchange enforcement and the management/permissions surface for clients with no error, test, or migration note in the diff; any code path that does reach these methods under the V2 feature gets an UnsupportedOperationException (HTTP 500) instead of a permission decision or a 4xx.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff exercises the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope or isolates MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE: testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE and CONFIGURE in a single permission (line 359) before calling addComposites, and MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE (canMapClientScopeRoles, ClientPermissionsV2.java:101-103) is never granted or asserted anywhere in the diff's tests. A regression that wires canMapCompositeRoles or canMapClientScopeRoles to the wrong scope constant (or drops one from the schema) passes the suite; the client scope-mappings management endpoint would then silently deny or over-grant client-role mapping in production. The per-client VIEW-only grant path (hasPermission(client, VIEW), ClientPermissionsV2.java:82) is likewise never exercised in isolation — testViewAllClients only covers the all-clients VIEW grant.

[ADVISORY] The evaluate-permission-then-match-scope loop is copy-pasted three times in this new class (hasPermission(ClientModel,String) lines 224-234, hasPermission(String) lines 249-259, hasGrantedPermission lines 276-285) with drift already present: hasGrantedPermission re-fetches root.realmResourceServer() per resource and uses scope.equals(s) while the other two use an Arrays.asList singleton and expectedScopes.contains(s). Any fix to the scope-matching logic (e.g., handling multiple expected scopes or null scope sets) must be applied in three places; missing one yields inconsistent grant decisions between the per-client, all-clients, and listing-filter paths.

[ADVISORY] The new getClientByClientId fallback branch in resolveClient (lines 179-181) has no coverage: every test in the diff creates client permissions with the client UUID (e.g., PermissionClientTest line 359 uses myclient.getId()), and PermissionRESTTest.resourcesTest only exercises name-based resolution for USERS. A regression in the clientId lookup path (returning null and silently creating no resource, so the permission grants nothing) would ship undetected, since no test creates a Clients-type permission referenced by clientId the way resourcesTest does for users by username.

[ADVISORY] The schema-validation tests in permissionsTest cover only the USERS resource type (all three negative cases use AdminPermissionsSchema.USERS), and testSupportedPolicyTypes likewise only creates a USERS-type permission, so the newly added CLIENTS type and its six scopes have no validation coverage. A regression in the CLIENTS schema entry (a misspelled scope constant, a missing scope, or a wrong type-to-scope mapping) would not be caught: invalid scopes on Clients-type permissions would be accepted (or valid ones rejected) without any test failure, and the permission-creation API would drift from the schema silently.

[BUG] This hunk gates the role/client/group removal-cleanup listener behind Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ — behavior change untraceable to 'add Client resource type and scopes' — and its net effect combined with the new MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() override is that V2 mode has no working cleanup path for deleted clients, because the handler's target ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (ClientPermissionsV2.java:192-195) throws UnsupportedOperationException; deleting a client that has V2 permissions therefore never removes its Resource or permission rows. Every deletion of a permissioned client in a V2-enabled realm permanently accumulates an orphaned Resource (named by the dead client's id) plus its granted permissions in the realm resource server; the orphans are re-evaluated by getClientsWithPermission on every filtered client listing and persist in authorization listings, and the deletion-cleanup behavior change ships with zero test coverage — the PR's own testManageAllClients deletes only a client for which no permissions were ever created, so the gap is untested by construction.

[ADVISORY] getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is dead code — no method in this new class calls it — and it is the only consumer of the ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext and EvaluationContext imports, alongside the unused TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import (line 46), the unused Scope import (line 27), and the unused logger field (line 51). Readers of the V2 client evaluator assume token-exchange attribute evaluation (the kc.client.id attribute wiring) exists and is reachable here when it is not; the dead private method and its orphaned imports get carried through every future refactor of this security-sensitive class and mislead anyone auditing how V2 reaches authorization decisions.

[ADVISORY] The V2 overrides replace the entire per-client permission-management and token-exchange surface with UnsupportedOperationException throws (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRoles*Permission, manage/configure/viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions at lines 147-205), and the CLIENTS schema type defines no token-exchange scope, whereas before this diff V2 mode fell back to the inherited V1 clients() implementation where these paths evaluated (or denied) normally instead of crashing. A realm switched to the V2 feature loses client token-exchange authorization and per-client permission introspection with no migration path; any reachable caller — e.g., a token-exchange permission check that previously consulted the V1 fallback — now gets a 500 from the UnsupportedOperationException instead of a grant/deny decision, and there is no CLIENTS scope an administrator could grant to restore the behavior.

[ADVISORY] canMapClientScopeRoles and the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope it evaluates are implemented and registered in the CLIENTS resource type, but no test in this diff exercises that scope — PermissionClientTest uses only CONFIGURE, MANAGE, MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE and VIEW. A regression in the map-roles-client-scope path — such as evaluating the wrong scope constant or omitting it from the CLIENTS scope set — ships silently; it is the only one of the six Client scopes with neither positive nor negative coverage in this PR, while all five siblings gained both.

[ADVISORY] The evaluatePermission-then-scope-match block is copy-pasted three times within this new file (hasPermission(ClientModel,String) at 207-235, hasPermission(String) at 237-260, hasGrantedPermission at 274-286) and duplicates the same block already present in UserPermissionsV2. Any fix to how granted scopes are matched (deny-policy handling, decision strategy, same-realm guarding) must be applied in five places across two classes; updating one copy silently produces inconsistent decisions between the per-client, all-clients, and listing-filter paths — the classic drift the Users/Clients parallel implementations already exhibit.

[BUG] ClientPermissionsV2 hard-throws UnsupportedOperationException from getPermissions/isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled, so the existing /admin/realms/{r}/clients/{id}/permissions endpoints — which before this diff resolved through the inherited V1 ClientPermissions implementation (graceful no-op/empty map when no V1 resource server exists) — now return a 500 whenever the V2 root is selected. Any V1-era automation or console path calling the per-client permissions endpoints gets a 500 instead of the previous representation as soon as the fine-grained-authz implementation switches to V2 — an unversioned breaking change to the admin REST contract with no 4xx, feature guard, or migration signal.

[BUG] hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) evaluates only the client's own resource when one exists and consults the all-clients type resource only as a fallback when it is null, so type-level grants — the 'Also if it has permission to MANAGE/VIEW/CONFIGURE all clients' contract the javadocs added in this diff explicitly promise — are silently ignored for any client that has ever had an individual permission created. An admin granted MANAGE on all clients permanently loses manage/view/configure access to every client for which any per-client permission was ever created (the per-client resource survives permission deletion, so the shadowing is permanent), and a type-level NEGATIVE permission is likewise never evaluated for those clients — legal permission combinations evaluate to the wrong decision, fail-closed for grants and fail-open for denies.

[BUG] canViewClientScopes() is not overridden and inherits canView(), which lacks the type-level MANAGE path that the adjacent canManageClientScopes() and canView(ClientScopeModel) overrides in this same class both include. A caller granted only the all-clients MANAGE permission can create client scopes (requireManageClientScopes passes) and fetch them individually (canView(ClientScopeModel) returns true) but gets 403 from GET /admin/realms/{r}/client-scopes (requireViewClientScopes) — a manage-without-view capability combination the rest of this evaluator deliberately avoids.

[ADVISORY] The ClientRemovedEvent cleanup branch is wired to clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which this diff routes (via the new MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() override) to ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled — a method that unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException — while the new feature guard skips the branch entirely for V2 realms, leaving V2 client resources with no implemented removal path anywhere in the change. Deleting a client leaves its 'Clients'-type resource and attached permissions orphaned in the realm resource server forever; getClientsWithPermission keeps loading and fully evaluating these ghost resources on every client list, and because the guard skips the path under V2 the V2 test suite can never exercise or catch the gap (and if the guard's feature condition ever aligns with V2 selection, the same wiring turns client deletion into a 500).

[ADVISORY] The evaluate-permissions-and-match-scope loop is duplicated three times in the class (hasPermission(ClientModel,String), hasPermission(String), hasGrantedPermission) with already-divergent matching style (expectedScopes.contains vs scope.equals), and hasGrantedPermission re-resolves root.realmResourceServer() per resource although its only caller already holds `server` in scope. Any future change to the matching semantics (multi-scope checks, deny handling) must be replicated in three places and will silently drift, as the two styles already have; the redundant per-resource resource-server lookup adds a store call inside the getClientsWithPermission iteration.

[ADVISORY] The private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) method has no caller anywhere in the class (the only methods taking those parameters — canExchangeTo and the permission builders — throw UnsupportedOperationException), and the static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE is never referenced. Dead V1-copy code ships in the new class: readers and reviewers must verify the evaluation-context path is genuinely unreachable, and the orphaned TOKEN_EXCHANGE import signals the token-exchange permission story was copied in but not carried through for V2.

[ADVISORY] The per-client permission check's fallback calls getResourceTypeResource, which creates the 'Clients' type resource as a side effect of read-path permission checks, via an unsynchronized find-then-create with no unique constraint on (resource server, name) in the authorization store. Two concurrent first-time fine-grained requests in a realm can each create a 'Clients' resource, producing duplicate type resources that make the findByName-based lookups in hasPermission(String) ambiguous; the write also occurs on GET paths, and the sibling hasPermission(String) (find-only, null-means-no-grants) shows the read path does not need to create anything.

[ADVISORY] getClientsWithPermission runs a full policy evaluation (policy-store loads plus evaluator walk) for every 'Clients'-type resource on each client-list request, with no batching or caching across resources. The client-list endpoint's cost grows linearly with the number of individually-permissioned clients, each evaluation fanning out over its attached policies and associated policies — a scalability cliff on a hot admin path that this diff carries over from the V1 shape into the V2 implementation.

[ADVISORY] The MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope and the canMapClientScopeRoles() evaluator added in this diff are exercised by no test in the diff — the new tests cover only MANAGE, VIEW, CONFIGURE, MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE. A regression in the client-scope role-mapping check (e.g., binding the wrong scope constant among the three confusable map-roles variants) would silently allow or deny assigning client-scope roles through the admin API with no CI signal.

[BUG] The ClientRemovedEvent handler calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which now dispatches to ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled — a method that unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException — so deleting any client in a realm where the feature is enabled fails with a 500 and the client is not removed. Client deletion breaks across the admin API and in this PR's own suite (testManageAllClients removes a client; realm teardown deletes clients); since this handler is also the only removal-cleanup hook, the V2 permission resources of deleted clients are never cleaned up either.

[BUG] isPermissionsEnabled and setPermissionsEnabled throw UnsupportedOperationException, and the existing GET/PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/management/permissions endpoints call exactly these methods via AdminPermissions.management(), so once the V2 evaluator is selected the endpoint returns 500 where it previously returned the V1 permission state. The admin console's per-client permissions toggle and any API consumer of the management/permissions endpoint gets a 500 for every client; before this PR the same calls dispatched to the working V1 ClientPermissions implementation, so this is a regression introduced by the evaluator swap.

[BUG] canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles grant solely on the FGAP permission and drop the MANAGE_CLIENTS base-admin-role entitlement that the V1 evaluator honored, so enabling the feature silently revokes role-mapping rights from existing manage-clients administrators. An admin holding manage-clients who could previously map client roles gets 403 on the role-mapping endpoints the moment the V2 evaluator is selected, until someone creates an explicit MAP_ROLES permission; canManage/canView keep their base-role shortcuts, so the asymmetry reads as drift rather than design, and the entitlement change is not stated anywhere in the PR's objective.

[BUG] Wrapping the listener body in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) disables the role/client/group removal cleanup whenever the feature flag is off, whereas before this change setPermissionsEnabled(..., false) ran unconditionally on every removal event. A deployment that created fine-grained permissions and then turns the feature off accumulates orphaned permission resources for every subsequently deleted role/client/group, and the stale authorization data comes back live if the flag is re-enabled; this deletion-semantics change is unrelated to the PR's stated objective of adding a Clients resource type and is announced nowhere in it.

[ADVISORY] ClientPermissionsV2 carries dead scaffolding from the copied V1 implementation: the private getEvaluationContext method has no caller in the class, the TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import (line 46) is unused, and the logger field (line 51) is never used. The next maintainer pays for dead code that implies a token-exchange evaluation path exists when it was stubbed out; deleting the method, the import and the field removes ~15 lines with zero behavior change.

[ADVISORY] The evaluate-permissions-then-match-scope loop is written out three times in the same class (hasPermission(ClientModel,String), hasPermission(String), hasGrantedPermission), differing only in how the resource is obtained, and each copy allocates Arrays.asList(scope) for a single-element match. Any fix to the scope-matching logic (multiple expected scopes, empty scope sets) must be applied in three places and will drift; a single hasScope(Collection<Permission>, String) helper deletes roughly 20 lines.

[ADVISORY] canMapClientScopeRoles and the new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope have no test in this diff — no test grants the scope or exercises the client-scope role-mapping path, and no test covers negative (Logic.NEGATIVE) permissions for the Clients type. A regression in the map-roles-client-scope evaluation (wrong scope constant, inverted check) ships undetected; the sibling MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE paths are tested in PermissionClientTest, so the gap is cheap to close with one more case.

[ADVISORY] The CLIENTS resource type ships without any token-exchange scope and canExchangeTo/exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException, so the per-client token-exchange delegation that V1 client permissions provided silently disappears once the V2 evaluator is selected. Deployments relying on V1 FGAP token-exchange delegation lose the capability on feature upgrade with no migration path or warning, and any remaining caller of canExchangeTo (e.g. token-exchange grant evaluation) now fails at runtime instead of evaluating a policy; the unused TOKEN_EXCHANGE import and orphaned getEvaluationContext in this class are the fossils of that dropped path.

[BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles return hasPermission(client, scope) only — there is no hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) check and no canManage(client) short-circuit — while canConfigure(client) and canManage(client) in the same class deliberately keep that implication. With the V2 feature enabled, an admin holding the manage-clients admin role — or holding an FGAP MANAGE grant on the client — gets false from canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles (hasPermission returns false whenever no explicit MAP_ROLES-family grant exists, including in realms with no FGAP data at all, since realmResourceServer() is null or no policy matches), so mapping that client's roles or composites to users returns 403 for admins who could perform the operation before V2; the intra-class asymmetry with canConfigure(client) indicates the omission is unintentional rather than a least-privilege design choice.

[ADVISORY] The ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent cleanup in AdminPermissions.registerListener is now gated on the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ flag, and the V2 evaluator provides no replacement cleanup path — ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. On a server running with the V2 feature enabled (V1 flag off), deleting a client that has FGAP V2 grants leaves its per-client resource (named by the client UUID) and its scope permissions orphaned in the realm resource server permanently; getClientsWithPermission keeps iterating these dead resources via findByType on every filtered client listing, and no code in this diff ever removes them, so authorization data accumulates garbage for every deleted principal.

[ADVISORY] ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException while the class retains dead token-exchange scaffolding — the private getEvaluationContext helper and the TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import are never used. On a V2-enabled server, a token-exchange flow that consults client permissions through the shared MgmtPermissions.clients() evaluator gets a 500 from UnsupportedOperationException instead of an allow/deny decision (V1 evaluated the same request), so enabling V2 breaks token-exchange authorization at runtime rather than denying it cleanly; the unused scaffolding misleads the next maintainer into believing the V2 token-exchange path is implemented.

[BUG] With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled, deleting any client throws UnsupportedOperationException and the DELETE returns 500: the ClientRemovedEvent branch added in this diff calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() (added in this diff) returns ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (ClientPermissionsV2.java:192-195, this diff) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException — AdminPermissions.management() selects MgmtPermissionsV2 when the feature is enabled (MgmtPermissionsV2 is package-private and can only be constructed there, and the diff's own REST tests prove V2 is active in the admin path), so the listener routes the cleanup into the throwing stub. Every client deletion in a realm with the feature enabled fails with a 500; the diff's own testManageAllClients performs exactly this deletion (PermissionClientTest.java:274) and cannot pass with the listener wired, so the diff is internally inconsistent — either that test is red as submitted or the cleanup branch is dead code; no test in the diff asserts the cleanup behavior that would disambiguate which.

[ADVISORY] Feature-gating the removal-cleanup listener (cleanup now runs only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, and previously-unconditional V1 cleanup is skipped when it is disabled) is a behavioral change with zero test coverage: no test in the diff asserts that removing a role/client/group cleans up, or intentionally skips, associated permissions. A regression in removal cleanup (orphaned permission resources after entity deletion, or the UnsupportedOperationException routing on the client branch) lands silently; the only entity removal in the diff's tests is testManageAllClients's client delete (PermissionClientTest.java:274), which asserts only that the client is gone. Test files checked: PermissionClientTest.java, PermissionRESTTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java, AbstractPermissionTest.java — none reference the listener or cleanup-on-removal.

[ADVISORY] canMapClientScopeRoles and the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope added in this diff have no test: no test in the diff grants map-roles-client-scope or triggers the endpoint that consults it. A regression in the map-roles-client-scope path (wrong scope constant, inverted check) ships undetected, and the new scope constant reaches the permissions API unvalidated. Checked: PermissionClientTest.java (testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants only MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE and CONFIGURE), PermissionRESTTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java, AbstractPermissionTest.java — none reference MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE.

[ADVISORY] The V2 ClientScopeModel evaluator methods (canManageClientScopes, canManage(ClientScopeModel), canView(ClientScopeModel)) are new logic with no coverage: no test in the diff exercises the /client-scopes admin endpoints (list/create/update/delete client scopes) as a permission-holding admin. The VIEW-vs-MANAGE distinction for client scopes (an admin with only schema VIEW listing client scopes, or schema MANAGE creating them) is unverified; the diff's tests only touch a client's default-client-scopes subresource, which routes through canView/canManage(ClientModel), so a regression in these overrides ships silently. Checked: PermissionClientTest.java, PermissionRESTTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java, AbstractPermissionTest.java.

[ADVISORY] testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE and CONFIGURE on the client (plus MAP_ROLES on the user) in a single shot, so the addComposites success cannot be attributed to MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE and no negative test isolates it. A regression where the composite-role check consults CONFIGURE or MAP_ROLES instead of MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE still passes, and the scope-to-endpoint mapping for map-roles-composite — the core contract this PR introduces — is verified only in the everything-granted configuration; granting MAP_ROLES without MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE should still deny addComposites but that denial is never asserted.

[BUG] Client/role/group deletion in V2-mode deployments no longer removes the entity's fine-grained-permission data: the only cleanup hook (this removal-event listener) is now skipped whenever the V1 flag ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is off, and when the listener does run against V2 management it reaches ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which throws UnsupportedOperationException — so no code path on entity deletion ever removes the per-entity resources, scopes, and policies that V2 creates via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource. Every client deleted in a realm running the V2 schema (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, V1 flag off) leaves orphaned resource/policy rows in the realm's admin-permissions resource server; getClientsWithPermission (ClientPermissionsV2.java:124-145) keeps scanning and running full permission evaluation for every orphaned 'Clients'-typed resource on each filtered client listing, so evaluation cost grows with every deleted client and stale client IDs are returned in the granted set; the same accumulation applies to roles and groups through the same gate, and to deployments that disable the FGAP feature after creating permissions (deletions during the disabled window orphan rows that previously were cleaned up).

[BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException but remains reachable from the ClientRemovedEvent listener (AdminPermissions.java:92) whenever the V1 flag ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled alongside the V2 feature, because AdminPermissions.management() then returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whose new clients() override selects this throwing evaluator. Deleting any client in a realm with both FGAP features enabled (a reachable configuration during V1-to-V2 evaluation, since no profile conflict is declared) fails: the UnsupportedOperationException propagates out of the synchronous removal event and the delete request returns a 500 with the deletion rolled back — a regression from the review base, where the listener reached the V1 ClientPermissions cleanup and client deletion succeeded.

[BUG] Gating the removal listener on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (the legacy V1 feature) disables all permission cleanup when only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, so deleting a client that has fine-grained permissions leaves its per-client 'Clients' resource (created via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource, named by the client id) orphaned in the realm resource server while the DELETE returns success. In every V2-only realm, each deleted client that ever had a permission granted leaves a ghost authorization resource: ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission (ClientPermissionsV2.java:138-142) keeps running a full policy evaluation for every dead resource on each admin client listing (cost grows with the corpse count), the permissions resource listing shows entries for clients that no longer exist, and no log or error ever surfaces the skipped cleanup.

[BUG] The gate checks the legacy ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature while management() dispatches to the V2 implementation whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, so with both features enabled the gate passes and the ClientRemovedEvent handler calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (ClientPermissionsV2.java:192-195), which throws UnsupportedOperationException and turns client deletion into a 500. On a server configured with both fine-grained-authz features enabled, every DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id} fails with a raw UnsupportedOperationException (500) instead of completing or returning a 4xx; the gate only protects this path if the two features are mutually exclusive, an invariant nothing in this diff establishes or enforces.

[ADVISORY] The evaluate-permission-and-match-scope loop is hand-copied three times in this class (hasPermission(ClientModel,String) lines 224-232, hasPermission(String) lines 249-257, hasGrantedPermission lines 276-283), and the copies already diverge: hasGrantedPermission omits the isAdminSameRealm and realmResourceServer-null guards the other two enforce, relying on each caller to remember them. The next change to the permission decision (a new guard, a scope-matching fix) must be replicated in three places inside a security-decision class; missing one silently diverges per-client, all-clients, and listing-path results. Extracting one guarded helper (hasGrantedPermission is already most of it) deletes roughly 20 lines.

[ADVISORY] getEvaluationContext is dead code — no method in the class calls it (its only natural caller, canExchangeTo at lines 147-150, throws UnsupportedOperationException) — and it sits beside an unused static import of TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46) and an unused logger field (line 51), all copy-paste residue from the V1 ClientPermissions implementation. Whoever implements V2 token-exchange support later will read the pre-built evaluation context (with its kc.client.id attribute) as the intended wiring and reuse a context shaped for the V1 flow; deleting the method, the import, and the logger removes ~15 lines with zero behavior change.

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The removal-event cleanup is now gated solely on the V1 flag (Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so deleting a client in a realm running the V2 feature (which this PR's ClientPermissionsV2 serves) performs no authorization cleanup at all, because the only handler would call ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (ClientPermissionsV2.java:193-195), which throws UnsupportedOperationException. The Resource and permission policies created for a client via getOrCreateResource/resolveClient (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:175-184, exercised by PermissionClientTest's createPermission calls) are orphaned forever in the realm's admin-permissions resource server when the client is deleted: getClientsWithPermission keeps iterating dead resources on every filtered client listing, the store accumulates stale entries with no V2 API to purge them (getPermissions/setPermissionsEnabled throw), and the same skip applies to realms that enabled V1 FGAP earlier and later turned the flag off. The diff ships the write path for client authorization resources without any delete path.

[ADVISORY] The private method getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) has zero call sites in the class (canExchangeTo at line 148 throws instead of using it), making it dead code together with the ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext/EvaluationContext imports and the unused logger field at line 51. Future maintainers reading the class can assume a token-exchange evaluation context exists and is wired up, when it is not; deleting the method removes 11 lines and three imports with no behavior change.

[ADVISORY] The CLIENTS resource type silently drops the token-exchange capability that V1 client permissions support: AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:70) omits the token-exchange scope, canExchangeTo/exchangeToPermission and the whole V1 per-client permission-management surface (isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) throw UnsupportedOperationException, and the static import of TOKEN_EXCHANGE at line 46 is unused — corroborating that the scope was considered and dropped without a replacement. Realms migrating from V1 fine-grained authz to V2 silently lose token-exchange enforcement and the management/permissions surface for clients with no error, test, or migration note in the diff; any code path that does reach these methods under the V2 feature gets an UnsupportedOperationException (HTTP 500) instead of a permission decision or a 4xx.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that the new V2 CLIENTS resource type omits any token-exchange-related scope (AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS scopes are CONFIGURE/MANAGE/MAP_ROLES/MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE/VIEW only) and that ClientPermissionsV2 explicitly disables several previously-supported client-permission operations by overriding methods like canExchangeTo/exchangeToPermission/mapRolesPermission/managePermission/configurePermission/viewPermission/isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled/resource/getPermissions to throw UnsupportedOperationException. It also includes an unused static import of TOKEN_EXCHANGE in ClientPermissionsV2, indicating token-exchange was at least contemplated. However, the diff alone does not prove this is a correctness/security defect (it could be an intentional V2 scope reduction and those methods may be unreachable under V2); what is verifiable is an architectural/migration gap and potential runtime risk if any existing code path calls these methods under V2.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] This hunk gates the role/client/group removal-cleanup listener behind Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ — behavior change untraceable to 'add Client resource type and scopes' — and its net effect combined with the new MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() override is that V2 mode has no working cleanup path for deleted clients, because the handler's target ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (ClientPermissionsV2.java:192-195) throws UnsupportedOperationException; deleting a client that has V2 permissions therefore never removes its Resource or permission rows. Every deletion of a permissioned client in a V2-enabled realm permanently accumulates an orphaned Resource (named by the dead client's id) plus its granted permissions in the realm resource server; the orphans are re-evaluated by getClientsWithPermission on every filtered client listing and persist in authorization listings, and the deletion-cleanup behavior change ships with zero test coverage — the PR's own testManageAllClients deletes only a client for which no permissions were ever created, so the gap is untested by construction.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the removal-cleanup listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener now runs only when Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, and within that path it still handles ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). The same PR introduces MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() which returns ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) to unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException. Therefore, in the V2 permissions implementation, the client-removal cleanup path invoked by the listener will blow up instead of disabling/removing permissions, which can prevent cleanup of authorization artifacts associated with deleted clients.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ClientPermissionsV2 hard-throws UnsupportedOperationException from getPermissions/isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled, so the existing /admin/realms/{r}/clients/{id}/permissions endpoints — which before this diff resolved through the inherited V1 ClientPermissions implementation (graceful no-op/empty map when no V1 resource server exists) — now return a 500 whenever the V2 root is selected. Any V1-era automation or console path calling the per-client permissions endpoints gets a 500 instead of the previous representation as soon as the fine-grained-authz implementation switches to V2 — an unversioned breaking change to the admin REST contract with no 4xx, feature guard, or migration signal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() return a new ClientPermissionsV2 implementation. In ClientPermissionsV2, several previously-implemented API methods are overridden to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`, including `getPermissions(ClientModel)`, `isPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel)`, and `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)`. Any existing code paths/endpoints that call these methods when the V2 permission root is selected will now fail at runtime with an unchecked exception (likely surfacing as HTTP 500), which is a behavior-breaking change introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) evaluates only the client's own resource when one exists and consults the all-clients type resource only as a fallback when it is null, so type-level grants — the 'Also if it has permission to MANAGE/VIEW/CONFIGURE all clients' contract the javadocs added in this diff explicitly promise — are silently ignored for any client that has ever had an individual permission created. An admin granted MANAGE on all clients permanently loses manage/view/configure access to every client for which any per-client permission was ever created (the per-client resource survives permission deletion, so the shadowing is permanent), and a type-level NEGATIVE permission is likewise never evaluated for those clients — legal permission combinations evaluate to the wrong decision, fail-closed for grants and fail-open for denies.

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, the code looks up a per-client `Resource` by name `client.getId()` and, if found, evaluates permissions only against that resource. The all-clients type resource (`AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`) is consulted only when the per-client resource lookup returns `null`. Therefore, any type-level grant/deny on the CLIENTS resource type is ignored for clients that already have an individual resource, contradicting the new javadocs stating V2 should also allow via `MANAGE/VIEW/CONFIGURE` “all clients” permissions. This yields incorrect authorization decisions (type-level grants not applied; type-level negatives not applied) for those clients.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] canViewClientScopes() is not overridden and inherits canView(), which lacks the type-level MANAGE path that the adjacent canManageClientScopes() and canView(ClientScopeModel) overrides in this same class both include. A caller granted only the all-clients MANAGE permission can create client scopes (requireManageClientScopes passes) and fetch them individually (canView(ClientScopeModel) returns true) but gets 403 from GET /admin/realms/{r}/client-scopes (requireViewClientScopes) — a manage-without-view capability combination the rest of this evaluator deliberately avoids.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2` class, `canView()` is overridden to return only `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` and does not include a type-level `MANAGE` permission path. However, adjacent overrides in the same class *do* treat type-level `MANAGE` as sufficient for related client-scope operations (`canManageClientScopes()` returns `hasPermission(MANAGE)`, and `canView(ClientScopeModel)` returns `hasPermission(VIEW) || hasPermission(MANAGE)`). adjudication.rationale: In `PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient`, the test grants multiple client scopes at once (`Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE)`) via `createPermission(client, myclient.getId(), clientsType, ...)` and then asserts `addComposites(...)` succeeds. Because `CONFIGURE` and `MAP_ROLES` are also granted alongside `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`, the test does not isolate that `addComposites` is actually gated by the new `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` scope, nor does it include a negative assertion that `addComposites` is forbidden when `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` is missing. This is a concrete, diff-grounded testing gap for the new scope-to-endpoint contract introduced by the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Client/role/group deletion in V2-mode deployments no longer removes the entity's fine-grained-permission data: the only cleanup hook (this removal-event listener) is now skipped whenever the V1 flag ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is off, and when the listener does run against V2 management it reaches ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which throws UnsupportedOperationException — so no code path on entity deletion ever removes the per-entity resources, scopes, and policies that V2 creates via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource. Every client deleted in a realm running the V2 schema (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, V1 flag off) leaves orphaned resource/policy rows in the realm's admin-permissions resource server; getClientsWithPermission (ClientPermissionsV2.java:124-145) keeps scanning and running full permission evaluation for every orphaned 'Clients'-typed resource on each filtered client listing, so evaluation cost grows with every deleted client and stale client IDs are returned in the granted set; the same accumulation applies to roles and groups through the same gate, and to deployments that disable the FGAP feature after creating permissions (deletions during the disabled window orphan rows that previously were cleaned up).

adjudication.rationale: The diff wraps the only deletion cleanup listener in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java), so when that V1 feature flag is off the `RoleRemovedEvent`/`ClientRemovedEvent`/`GroupRemovedEvent` handlers no longer run at all—meaning no permission cleanup happens on deletion in that configuration. Separately, in V2 the new `ClientPermissionsV2` explicitly throws `UnsupportedOperationException` for `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` (and other cleanup-related methods), so even if the listener were invoked against a V2 `management(...).clients()` instance, it would fail to clean up. Meanwhile, V2 adds a `CLIENTS` resource type and client resource resolution/creation (`AdminPermissionsSchema` adds `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE`, `CLIENTS`, `resolveClient`, and includes it in the schema map), and `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission` iterates *all* `Clients`-typed resources in the store, so orphaned resources would be repeatedly scanned and could yield stale client IDs via `resource.getName()`. This matches the finding’s core claim that deletions can leave orphaned authz data and incur growing evaluation cost.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException but remains reachable from the ClientRemovedEvent listener (AdminPermissions.java:92) whenever the V1 flag ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled alongside the V2 feature, because AdminPermissions.management() then returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whose new clients() override selects this throwing evaluator. Deleting any client in a realm with both FGAP features enabled (a reachable configuration during V1-to-V2 evaluation, since no profile conflict is declared) fails: the UnsupportedOperationException propagates out of the synchronous removal event and the delete request returns a 500 with the deletion rolled back — a regression from the review base, where the listener reached the V1 ClientPermissions cleanup and client deletion succeeded.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a concrete inconsistency: the synchronous removal listener in AdminPermissions.onEvent (now gated by Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false) for ClientRemovedEvent, while the newly added ClientPermissionsV2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) to unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException. MgmtPermissionsV2 also now overrides clients() to return ClientPermissionsV2. However, the finding’s key reachability claim (that AdminPermissions.management() will return MgmtPermissionsV2 in a configuration where the listener is active, e.g., “V1 + V2 both enabled”) cannot be verified from this diff because the selection logic for management()/feature interactions is not shown. So the crash/rollback behavior is plausible but not provable from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Gating the removal listener on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (the legacy V1 feature) disables all permission cleanup when only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, so deleting a client that has fine-grained permissions leaves its per-client 'Clients' resource (created via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource, named by the client id) orphaned in the realm resource server while the DELETE returns success. In every V2-only realm, each deleted client that ever had a permission granted leaves a ghost authorization resource: ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission (ClientPermissionsV2.java:138-142) keeps running a full policy evaluation for every dead resource on each admin client listing (cost grows with the corpse count), the permissions resource listing shows entries for clients that no longer exist, and no log or error ever surfaces the skipped cleanup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff wraps the ProviderEventListener cleanup logic in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java), so if that flag is off the removal events no longer call `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)` for Role/Client/Group deletions. At the same time, this PR introduces V2 client resource-type authorization (`AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE`, `resolveClient`, inclusion in schema map) and adds `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission` which iterates *all* stored `Clients` resources (`resourceStore.findByType(...)`) and runs permission evaluation on each. There is no V2-side deletion cleanup shown; moreover `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...)` is explicitly `UnsupportedOperationException`, so the existing cleanup mechanism is not available for V2. This makes orphaned per-client `Clients` resources after client deletion a real risk, and the iteration/evaluation in `getClientsWithPermission` would scale with those leftovers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The gate checks the legacy ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature while management() dispatches to the V2 implementation whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, so with both features enabled the gate passes and the ClientRemovedEvent handler calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (ClientPermissionsV2.java:192-195), which throws UnsupportedOperationException and turns client deletion into a 500. On a server configured with both fine-grained-authz features enabled, every DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id} fails with a raw UnsupportedOperationException (500) instead of completing or returning a 4xx; the gate only protects this path if the two features are mutually exclusive, an invariant nothing in this diff establishes or enforces.

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener(), all removal-event handling is now gated only by Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ. Inside that block, ClientRemovedEvent triggers management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). This diff introduces MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returning a ClientPermissionsV2 instance, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...) is overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException. The diff does not establish/enforce that ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and a V2 mode are mutually exclusive, so in a configuration where the listener runs but management() yields the V2 permissions implementation, client deletion cleanup would throw and likely surface as a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The evaluate-permission-and-match-scope loop is hand-copied three times in this class (hasPermission(ClientModel,String) lines 224-232, hasPermission(String) lines 249-257, hasGrantedPermission lines 276-283), and the copies already diverge: hasGrantedPermission omits the isAdminSameRealm and realmResourceServer-null guards the other two enforce, relying on each caller to remember them. The next change to the permission decision (a new guard, a scope-matching fix) must be replicated in three places inside a security-decision class; missing one silently diverges per-client, all-clients, and listing-path results. Extracting one guarded helper (hasGrantedPermission is already most of it) deletes roughly 20 lines.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2` class, the “evaluate permissions then match scopes” logic is duplicated in three methods: `hasPermission(ClientModel,String)`, `hasPermission(String)`, and `hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String)`. The duplication is verifiable in the diff (each iterates `permissions` and then nested iterates `permission.getScopes()`). The finding is also correct that these copies already differ in their guarding: `hasPermission(...)` methods enforce `root.isAdminSameRealm()` and `server == null` checks, while `hasGrantedPermission(...)` does neither and directly calls `root.realmResourceServer()` and uses it (safe today only because its current caller `getClientsWithPermission` checks those guards first). This is a maintainability/consistency risk in a security-decision class, but not a demonstrable functional bug from the diff alone because current call paths satisfy the missing guards.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getEvaluationContext is dead code — no method in the class calls it (its only natural caller, canExchangeTo at lines 147-150, throws UnsupportedOperationException) — and it sits beside an unused static import of TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46) and an unused logger field (line 51), all copy-paste residue from the V1 ClientPermissions implementation. Whoever implements V2 token-exchange support later will read the pre-built evaluation context (with its kc.client.id attribute) as the intended wiring and reuse a context shaped for the V1 flow; deleting the method, the import, and the logger removes ~15 lines with zero behavior change.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2` class, `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel authorizedClient, AccessToken token)` is never invoked by any method in the diff. The only likely callers (`canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, etc.) all immediately throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, and no other code references the method. Additionally, the static import `AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE` and the `private static final Logger logger` field are present but unused anywhere in the class. This is diff-verifiable copy/paste residue and can be removed without behavioral change.
